clue.text: Nasty officer's last to tease in mess!

indicators.note: in places the officer's final letter plus the word for tease inside the word for mess

parts.note: a mess or muddle can be called a hole, as in 'in a hole'

indicators.note: last picks only the final letter of the word officer's

parts.note: to rib someone is to tease them

explanation.surface: An exclamation about a nasty officer who teases subordinates in the mess.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mess' looks like the officers' dining room, but it is HOLE (a fix), and 'last' takes the R of 'officer's'.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words describe something unpleasant or offensive; they are plain synonyms.

clue.text: Entertainment it's unusual to repeat

indicators.note: unusual tells us the letters of 'to repeat' come in an odd order here

explanation.surface: Someone remarks that it is rare for a show to be repeated.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unusual' rearranges TO REPEAT; 'it's' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A light opera is a form of stage entertainment, so the definition names its category.

clue.text: Parson's position on ambassador leaving bully's joint

parts.note: re means on or concerning

indicators.note: leaving says the ambassador's letters depart from the bully's word

parts.note: to hector is to bully, so a bully is a hector
HE is His Excellency, the title of an ambassador
the hip is a joint of the body

explanation.surface: A clergyman's stance on a diplomat who walks out on a bully's hangout.
explanation.walkthrough: 'joint' looks like a dive or bar, but it is the body's HIP; 'leaving' drops HE from HECTORS to leave CTORS.
explanation.definitionFit: A rector is a parish priest, and the office he holds is described by this word for his post.

clue.text: One who needs notice before carrying out a stick-up?

definitions.text: One who needs notice before carrying out a stick-up?

parts.words: One who needs notice before carrying out a stick-up?
parts.note: reads like a robber wanting warning before a hold-up, but notice is a printed poster he sticks up on a wall

explanation.surface: An oddly courteous robber who wants advance warning before a hold-up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stick-up' suggests armed robbery; here it is literally sticking up a printed notice.
explanation.definitionFit: The person who pastes up advertisements needs a printed notice before he can stick it to a wall.

clue.text: Issue Greek character raised, supporting English valet

indicators.note: in a down clue the supporting piece sits below the English valet

parts.note: a valet is a manservant, a man

indicators.note: raised in a down clue means the Greek letter is turned upwards, read from bottom to top

parts.note: eta is a letter of the Greek alphabet

explanation.surface: A Greek man lifted up and helping an English manservant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'raised' turns ETA to ATE, placed under E MAN.
explanation.definitionFit: To issue is to flow or come forth, the same verb sense as the answer.

clue.text: Shrub graduate removed from boundaries of Asian capital

indicators.note: the graduate's letters are taken away from the outside edges of the capital city's name

parts.note: Manila is the capital of the Philippines
MA is a Master of Arts, a graduate

explanation.surface: A plant with no graduate in the outskirts of an Asian city.
explanation.walkthrough: The M and A at the edges of MANILA spell MA, the graduate, so removing them leaves the core.
explanation.definitionFit: The indigo plant is a tropical shrub yielding blue dye, known by this name.

clue.text: Ringer's understudy

definitions.meaning: a ringer is a person who looks exactly like another; the 's stands for 'is'
an understudy can stand in for an actor, playing the role as a substitute

explanation.definitionFit: A dead ringer is a lookalike, and an actor's stand-in is likewise called by this word.

clue.text: Hormone hidden at home

parts.note: something hidden is kept secret
in means at home, as in 'staying in'

explanation.surface: A hormone tucked away in a house.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hidden' looks like a hidden-word signal but is SECRET.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a digestive hormone released by the small intestine to stimulate the pancreas.

clue.text: Tree bishop, possibly, planted to left of wood

indicators.note: in an across clue, placed to the left means coming first, before the wood

parts.note: a bishop is one example of a chess man, hence 'possibly'
a grove is a small wood

explanation.surface: A churchman planting a tree beside a woodland.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bishop' points to the church, but it is a chess piece, a MAN.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a tropical tree growing in coastal swamps, so the definition names its kind.

clue.text: Writer going into case, one with some point

definitions.meaning: a writing implement that is kept in its own case, as schoolchildren carry
something sharpened to a point for drawing or writing

explanation.definitionFit: A wooden writing stick is stored in a case and has a sharpened tip, fitting both descriptions.

clue.text: Non-sailor taking posh bachelors into dance

indicators.note: into says the posh and bachelors letters go inside the dance

parts.note: a ländler is an Austrian folk dance in triple time
U means upper-class or posh
B is bachelor, so two Bs are bachelors

explanation.surface: A landsman drawing upper-class single men onto the dance floor.
explanation.walkthrough: LANDLER is an Austrian country dance, a forerunner of the waltz.
explanation.definitionFit: A landlubber is someone unused to the sea, the opposite of a seasoned sailor.

clue.text: Move around — it's cooler

definitions.meaning: to move something about, as with a spoon

explanation.definitionFit: Stir means to mix by moving around, and it is also slang for jail, like cooler.

clue.text: One's given the treatment in case? Quite the opposite

definitions.text: One's given the treatment in case? Quite the opposite

parts.words: One's given the treatment in case? Quite the opposite
parts.note: the opposite of someone treated while staying inside a hospital ward is someone treated while living outside

explanation.surface: A remark about someone receiving treatment, perhaps as a precaution.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in case' reads as 'as a precaution', but it means inside the hospital, an inpatient; the opposite is the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A hospital patient who attends for treatment without staying overnight is the reverse of a resident patient.

clue.text: Points used to advantage, possibly in magazines

definitions.meaning: arguments or facts that can be used to win a debate
cartridges or shells, which may be loaded in gun magazines

explanation.definitionFit: Debating points are figuratively ammo, and the literal bullets are stored in magazines.

clue.text: List of facts in Urdu possibly giving grounds for charge

parts.note: Urdu is one example of an Indic language, hence 'possibly'
a table is an organised list of facts or figures

explanation.surface: An Urdu fact sheet that may give grounds for a criminal charge.
explanation.walkthrough: Indic is the family of Indian languages including Urdu; 'in' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: An offence that can be formally prosecuted gives grounds for a charge in law.

clue.text: Ship's officer carrying revolutionary weapon

indicators.note: carrying means the officer holds the revolutionary inside him

parts.note: a mate is an officer on a merchant ship
Che Guevara is the archetypal revolutionary

explanation.surface: A ship's officer armed with a revolutionary's weapon.
explanation.definitionFit: A broad heavy blade used for cutting cane or fighting is a weapon.

clue.text: Soak temperate shrub friend's imported

indicators.note: imported means the friend has taken the shrub into himself

parts.note: a mate is a friend; the 's stands for 'has'
acer, the maple genus, grows in temperate regions

explanation.surface: Soaking a hardy shrub that a friend brought in from abroad.
explanation.walkthrough: 'temperate' looks like an adjective about the soak; it qualifies ACER.
explanation.definitionFit: To macerate is to soften something by soaking it in liquid.

clue.text: Second insect beginning to nark a little

parts.note: a midge is a small biting insect

indicators.note: beginning to picks the opening letter of the word nark

explanation.surface: A second insect starts to irritate slightly.
explanation.definitionFit: A smidgen is a tiny amount, so 'a little' captures it as a quantity.

clue.text: Calm quality a particular loch unexpectedly displayed

parts.note: even can express surprise, as in 'he even smiled', so it means unexpectedly
Loch Ness is a particular Scottish loch

explanation.surface: A Scottish loch surprisingly showing a calm surface.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unexpectedly' looks like an anagram signal but gives EVEN; 'displayed' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Being level and unruffled is a calm quality, hence smoothness or equanimity.

clue.text: Escorted objective woman employed outside

indicators.note: outside means the word for employed wraps around the woman

parts.note: used means employed
her is the objective case of she

explanation.surface: A woman with clear goals hired to work outdoors was shown the way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'objective' suggests a purposeful woman; it is the grammatical case.
explanation.definitionFit: To usher is to escort someone to a seat, so the past tense matches 'escorted'.

clue.text: Analogy made by fellow doctor, with capital in north

annotationWithheld.clue: Analogy made by fellow doctor, with capital in north

clue.text: Many a bore is lacking in strength

parts.note: M is the Roman numeral for a thousand, so many
an eagre is a tidal bore, a wave surging up a river

explanation.surface: Many a tedious person is feeble.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bore' suggests a tedious person; it is a tidal wave, EAGRE. 'is' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Meagre means scanty or poor, lacking in substance or strength.

clue.text: Train team identified in station announcement

indicators.note: an announcement is spoken, so the station's name is said out loud

parts.note: Crewe is a major railway junction station in Cheshire, England

explanation.surface: A railway team named over the station tannoy.
explanation.walkthrough: CREWE is a famous English railway junction town.
explanation.definitionFit: The staff who operate a train are its crew, the working team on board.

clue.text: Undertake renewed planting of trees far off?

indicators.note: off signals that the letters of 'of trees far' have gone off their usual order

explanation.surface: Planning to replant woods somewhere distant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'off' rearranges OF TREES FAR; it looks like part of 'far off'.
explanation.definitionFit: To replant a deforested area with trees is to restore its forest cover again.

clue.text: Head off tramp beginning to eye musical instrument

indicators.note: head off removes the first letter of the word for tramp

parts.note: a hobo is a tramp or vagrant

indicators.note: beginning to takes the first letter of eye

explanation.surface: A tramp heading off at the sight of a musical instrument.
explanation.definitionFit: The oboe is a double-reed woodwind instrument.

clue.text: Natural origin of bankruptcy — owing money all round

indicators.note: all round means the debt phrase surrounds the letter

parts.note: being in the red means owing money

indicators.note: origin of picks the first letter of bankruptcy

explanation.surface: A born tendency to go bust, with debts all around.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Natural' means innate, as an inbred trait is.
explanation.definitionFit: An inbred quality is innate, inborn and so natural.

clue.text: Tedious couple of notes on period costume

indicators.note: in an across clue, the notes on the costume come after it

parts.note: tire is an archaic word for attire, old-fashioned dress
so and me are two notes of the sol-fa scale
so and me are two notes of the sol-fa scale

explanation.surface: A dreary remark about a period drama's costumes.
explanation.walkthrough: TIRE is archaic for attire; SO and ME are sol-fa notes (doh, re, me...).
explanation.definitionFit: Tedious and tiresome both describe something dull and wearying.

clue.text: Ballerina touring Florida area is European

indicators.note: touring means the European goes round the area

parts.note: a Dane is a European, from Denmark
Florida lies in the SE (south-east) US

explanation.surface: A European ballerina touring Florida.
explanation.walkthrough: SE US is the region containing Florida; 'is' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A danseuse is a female ballet dancer, which a ballerina is.
